title: Distributed Coordination, Locks and Leader Election

nodes.label: Client applications
nodes.summary: Services that need a leader, a lock or shared configuration. They hold a session with the cluster and must handle losing it.

nodes.label: Coordination cluster
nodes.summary: A small replicated service (typically five replicas in Chubby) that stores small files or nodes, locks and sessions, and notifies clients of changes. Emphasis on availability and reliability, not throughput.

nodes.label: Master / leader
nodes.summary: The replica that serves all requests; elected by consensus. In Chubby it needs a majority vote plus promises not to elect another master for the master lease; a new one is typically elected in a few seconds.

nodes.label: Replicas (majority quorum)
nodes.summary: Copies of the small database; writes are acknowledged when they reach a majority. Raft's election safety: at most one leader per term.

nodes.label: Sessions and watches
nodes.summary: Clients keep a session through KeepAlives; ephemeral nodes vanish when it ends; watches or events notify clients of changes.

nodes.label: Locks and sequencers
nodes.summary: Advisory reader-writer locks; a holder can obtain a sequencer (lock name, mode, generation number) to present to the resource it protects. A lock-delay protects servers that cannot check sequencers.

nodes.label: Protected resource
nodes.summary: A storage or job server that checks the sequencer or fencing token of each request and rejects stale ones. The checking is our design; Chubby describes the mechanism.

nodes.label: Alternative: lock row in a database
nodes.summary: For low-stakes or single-tenant cases a conditional update on a database row can serve as a lease. It gives up consensus guarantees and notifications.

flows.name: Acquire a lock and use it

steps.caption: The client opens a session and keeps it alive.
It acquires the lock and asks for a sequencer.
The master records the lock state.
The change is replicated to a majority before it is acknowledged.
The client sends its requests to the protected resource, attaching the sequencer.
The resource checks the sequencer is still valid (or compares it with the highest it has seen).

flows.name: A lock holder pauses and wakes up late (failure)

steps.caption: The holder stops sending KeepAlives (for example it is paused); its session expires and the lock is released. If the lock was released because the holder failed or became inaccessible, a lock-delay can keep others from claiming it for a short time, for servers that cannot check sequencers.
After any lock-delay, another client acquires the lock with a higher generation number.
The first client resumes and sends a request with its old sequencer.
The resource sees the old sequencer is no longer valid and rejects the request.
The other replicas stop hearing from the master.
When the master lease expires they run an election; a new master is typically elected in a few seconds (values up to 30 s were reported), during which requests wait or fail.
Clients are told their session is in jeopardy and use a grace period before giving up (our summary of Chubby's session design).
Each waiter creates an ephemeral sequential node and watches only its predecessor.
When the holder releases or crashes, only the next waiter is notified.
